Serve a map

Source: R/serve.R
og_serve.Rd

Starts a server for an og_map() in the background of this R session, on host only (127.0.0.1: this computer), and opens the page. It answers while the console is idle: a map waits while R runs something else. og_stop() stops it. A grid's meta and a geojson layer's data are read once, when the server starts.

Usage

og_serve(
  map,
  port = NULL,
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  open = interactive(),
  query = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  verdicts = NULL,
  routes = NULL,
  wait = FALSE
)

og_stop(port = NULL)

Arguments

map

An og_map().

port

Where the server listens: a port, or NULL (the default) for 8790 or, when another program holds it, the next free port to 8889. A map served with no port replaces the last one served so, as a map served on a port replaces the one there; the address returned says where it is.

host

Where the server listens: 127.0.0.1, this computer only.

open

Whether to open the page: RStudio's Viewer when there is one, else a browser.

query

Settings for the first view, in the page's address (list(lang = "is", palette = "deep")).

notes

Opt-in, notes pinned on the map: the path of a .geojson file (in a folder that exists) where the server keeps them, made at the first note; NULL, none. The page then has a Notes group: "Add a note", a click on the map, a text, and the note is written to the file with the features under it; a reply joins a note's thread. og_notes() reads them in R and og_notes_add() answers. They are answered only for a page opened from this computer (as localhost, 127.0.0.1 or host), and never in a bundle.

verdicts

Opt-in, the readers' verdicts on features: the path of a .csv file (in a folder that exists) where the server keeps them, made at the first verdict; NULL, none. A layer whose popup has a verdict (og_layer()) then shows a button for each option in a feature's popup. Each answer is a row added to the file (when, the layer, the feature's value of the verdict's field, the option, the reader's line, the feature's title and place); a later one for the feature replaces it, and an empty answer withdraws it. og_verdicts() reads them. As the notes, answered only for a page opened from this computer, and never in a bundle.

routes

Opt-in, the map's own routes, for a page's own script (og_script()): a named list of functions, each answering /x/<name> (and /x/<name>/...) from the page by og.fetch(name, init), the name followed by a path and a query if any (og.fetch("marks/12?full=1")). A function is given one request, a list of method ("GET", "POST", ...), path (what follows its name, "/12"), query (the address's parameters, a named list, list(full = "1")) and body (a JSON body read, else its text, else NULL); it returns a list or a data frame, sent as JSON, a string, sent as text, or NULL, not found; an error is sent as its message. As the notes, answered only for a page opened from this computer. Keep each fast: the server answers one request at a time, and a slow route holds the tiles behind it (read a file once, and again only when it changes).

wait

Whether to keep serving until stopped (Ctrl-C, Esc in RStudio): TRUE in a script run by Rscript, whose map would otherwise go when the script ends. By default FALSE: the server answers while R is idle (in RStudio, while the console waits), and the call returns, so a script, a test or a document goes on.

Value

The page's address, invisibly.

Examples

# Opens a map in RStudio's Viewer (or a browser) when run by hand, e.g. by example(og_serve)
if (interactive()) {
  harbours <- og_layer(
    "harbours", "vector", label = "Harbours",
    tiles = og_tiles_table(og_example("dansk_harbours"), properties = "SI_HARB"),
    style = list(list(id = "harbours-fill", type = "fill", "source-layer" = "features",
                      paint = list("fill-color" = "#d9822b"))),
    popup = list(click = "harbours-fill", title = "SI_HARB")
  )
  m <- og_map(og_section("ref", "Reference", list(harbours)),
              title = "Danish harbours", view = list(center = c(10.5, 56), zoom = 7))
  og_serve(m)
  # again, opening on the ocean base map (it replaces the first):
  # og_serve(m, query = list(base = "ocean"))
  # with notes pinned on the map, kept in a file:
  # og_serve(m, notes = "harbour_notes.geojson"); og_notes("harbour_notes.geojson")
  # og_stop() # when done
}
